A.notes: A has a clear vertical-house idea: the rooms read as levels of the building, the roof breakfast lands naturally, and the drawn facade gives it a distinct signature. The typography and spacing are elegant and quiet, though some sections verge on too sparse and a few small text details feel delicate. From the scroll frames, the facade changes progressively with the room sections and the breakfast scene adds a small narrative beat; reduced-motion fallback appears intact.

B.notes: B has a strong opening line and a persuasive house/door motif that fits the restoration story well, with room facts presented more directly than A. But the normal full-page and mobile captures show large empty bands that make the scroll-driven layout feel less robust, even if the reduced-motion version is complete. The scroll strip suggests mostly reveal-based progression with a modest breakfast scene change, so motion reads as purposeful but not especially deep from the available evidence.

raw.why: A is the more coherent and better-resolved interpretation, with a stronger concept-to-layout connection and fewer signs of scroll mechanics undermining the page.
